definitions.explanation: The religion and philosophy founded by Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha). One of the major religions in Japan, influencing culture, art, architecture, and daily customs.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{仏教|ぶっきょう}の{寺|てら}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many Buddhist temples in Japan.

examples.japanese: {仏教|ぶっきょう}は6{世紀|せいき}に{日本|にほん}に{伝|つた}わった。
examples.english: Buddhism was introduced to Japan in the 6th century.

examples.japanese: {仏教|ぶっきょう}の{教|おし}えは{日本|にほん}の{文化|ぶんか}や{生活|せいかつ}{習慣|しゅうかん}に{深|ふか}く{根|ね}づいている。
examples.english: Buddhist teachings are deeply rooted in Japanese culture and daily customs.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仏教|ぶっきょう}の{教|おし}え (Buddhist teachings)
- {仏教|ぶっきょう}{寺院|じいん} (Buddhist temple)
- {仏教|ぶっきょう}{徒|と} (Buddhist, Buddhist follower)
- {大乗|だいじょう}{仏教|ぶっきょう} (Mahayana Buddhism)
- {仏教|ぶっきょう}{美術|びじゅつ} (Buddhist art)

CULTURAL NOTE: Most Japanese funerals follow Buddhist rites, and many families have a Buddhist altar ({仏壇|ぶつだん}) at home. However, everyday religious practice in Japan often blends Buddhist and Shinto elements.
